newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 13.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on December 13. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesian President Suharto said he did not want the relationship between the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the European Union (EU) to be damaged or disturbed by bilateral problems between nations of the two regional groupings.

The trials of 10 Indonesian activists for subversion began smoothly in the two Jakarta courts on Thursday but raised eyebrows for failing to refer to the previous allegations that the activists had masterminded the July 27 riots.
A study by leading academics has found Jakarta's middle class wants political and social change but does not want to take any risks.
State Secretary Murdiono said the government's body for the propagation of the state ideology Pancasila (BP-7) should be an institution of thinkers and intellectuals and not one of indoctrination.

Indonesian Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo has asked the European Union, Japan and the United States for more time to prepare its case after they complained to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) about Indonesia's controversial national car policy.
The Organisation of the Islamic Conference, whose foreign ministers are meeting in Jakarta this week, has supported Indonesia on its policies in the former Portuguese colony of East Timor.
